title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 196 (Right of person as to acts done for him without his authority)

content.overview: Section 196 provides that where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts. If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority.
content.glance: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another without that other’s knowledge or authority, the other may elect to ratify or disown the acts. If he ratifies them, the same effects follow as if they had been performed by his authority.
content.study: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts. If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority. Current-law framing: foundational rule of ratification of unauthorised acts.

sections.heading: Election to ratify or disown
sections.body: Where acts are done by one person on behalf of another, but without his knowledge or authority, he may elect to ratify or to disown such acts.

sections.heading: Effect of ratification
sections.body: If he ratify them, the same effects will follow as if they had been performed by his authority.

examples.title: Ratification of unauthorised acts
examples.body: Acts done on behalf of A without A’s knowledge or authority. A may ratify them, in which case the same effects follow as if they had been performed by his authority under Section 196.

hypotheticals.question: Acts are done on behalf of a person without his knowledge or authority. What may he do?
hypotheticals.analysis: He may elect to ratify or disown them. If he ratifies them, the same effects follow as if they had been performed by his authority, under Section 196.
